source: independent validator: research_clinic, validating a different researcher’s oilfield story

claims.statement: The planned project uses NOV’s existing drilling and control infrastructure in Navasota.
claims.text: The planned project uses NOV’s existing drilling and control infrastructure in Navasota.
claims.quote: Industry partner NOV Inc. will provide access to its Research and Development Test Center in Navasota, Texas, including advanced drilling infrastructure, automated control systems, and other technologies that will support mining-focused testing and validation.
claims.note: Future access and mining-focused testing are proposed; no completed synthetic mine is claimed.

claims.statement: Researchers plan to engineer mineral-bearing rock and place it in existing wells.
claims.text: Researchers plan to engineer mineral-bearing rock and place it in existing wells.
claims.quote: Researchers will be able to engineer mineral-bearing rock, place it in existing wells and repeatedly test new drilling, sensing and automation technologies, helping move promising innovations from laboratory research to field-scale demonstration and commercial use.
claims.note: The rock is engineered for testing. No claim that it was previously extracted, is economically valuable, or survives drilling unchanged.

claims.statement: The planned facility would support repeated tests of drilling, sensing and automation technologies.
claims.text: The planned facility would support repeated tests of drilling, sensing and automation technologies.
claims.quote: Researchers will be able to engineer mineral-bearing rock, place it in existing wells and repeatedly test new drilling, sensing and automation technologies, helping move promising innovations from laboratory research to field-scale demonstration and commercial use.
claims.note: Repeatability applies to tests and technology evaluation; it does not establish reuse or magical repair of one drilled specimen.

claims.statement: The project plans to adapt oil-and-gas automation and other technologies to test mining technology.
claims.text: The project plans to adapt oil-and-gas automation and other technologies to test mining technology.
claims.quote: The project will repurpose advanced technologies developed for the oil and gas industry — including automated drilling, high-bandwidth telemetry, fiber-optic sensing, robotics and digital twins — to test and improve technologies for critical-mineral extraction.
claims.note: No existing autonomous mining operation or successful extraction result is established.

claims.statement: Students and workers are intended to receive AI-enabled training, digital-twin simulations and hands-on experience.
claims.text: Students and workers are intended to receive AI-enabled training, digital-twin simulations and hands-on experience.
claims.quote: The project will also serve as a training ground for the next generation of engineers and mining professionals. Through AI-enabled training, digital-twin simulations and hands-on experience with advanced drilling and mining technologies, the project will prepare students and workers for careers using increasingly sophisticated mining systems.
claims.note: Training is planned. No named model, measured benefit, active trainees, or claim that AI learns from the trial data.

claims.statement: DOE selected the SMU Navasota project for award negotiations, announced September 9, 2026.
claims.text: DOE selected the SMU Navasota project for award negotiations, announced September 9, 2026.
claims.quote:
September 9, 2026
DOE’s Advanced Mining and Mineral Processing Technologies Office selected the following projects for award negotiations:
Southern Methodist University (HQ: Dallas, TX, project location: Navasota, Texas)
claims.note: Three exact source excerpts retain date, governing status sentence and project entry. No award execution or disbursement is established.

claims.statement: The two announcements describe future facility development and contain no completed-testbed report or test results.
claims.text: The two announcements describe future facility development and contain no completed-testbed report or test results.
claims.quote: This project will create the world’s first synthetic mine within an advanced drilling and sensing test facility to accelerate next generation mining technologies from lab concepts to field ready deployment. By repurposing a highly instrumented Texas drilling site, it will enable rigorous, repeatable, and safe testing of mining tools, workflows, and automation systems.
claims.note: Bounded absence finding after reading both complete release bodies. This is not evidence that no unpublished or later work exists.

claims.statement: The SMU project is named Well-to-Mine Proving Ground and is intended to test and validate mining technologies.
claims.text: The SMU project is named Well-to-Mine Proving Ground and is intended to test and validate mining technologies.
claims.quote: Salehi, the Herman Brown Chair in Mechanical Engineering in SMU’s Lyle School of Engineering, will lead the Well-to-Mine Proving Ground project, which will create the world’s first synthetic mine embedded within an advanced oil-and-gas drilling and sensing test facility. The facility will allow researchers to test and validate new mining technologies under controlled, real-world conditions.
claims.note: Purpose and project name only; do not use the superlative world’s first without qualification.

rejected.reason: Source says engineered mineral-bearing rock; it establishes neither economic value nor earlier extraction of this material.

rejected.claim: A drilled specimen resets to an intact specimen for another pass
rejected.reason: Repeated tests are supported; physical restoration or reuse of the same specimen is not.

rejected.claim: AI learns from the test results or already controls the mine
rejected.reason: AI-enabled training and a technology partnership do not specify such a model or operational control path.

rejected.claim: Workers are already training and mining tests have succeeded
rejected.reason: The releases describe planned facilities and future training, without completed trials or outcomes.
DOE’s controlling status is selection for award negotiations.

rejected.claim: The NOV cabin relocation demonstrates the new mine
rejected.reason: NOV republishes April 2023 reporting; this is historical site context, not 2026 project evidence.
